# Best Attendance & Payroll Software for Healthcare & Hospitals in India (2026)


October 19, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/best-attendance-payroll-software-for-healthcare-hospitals-in-india-2026/#respond)


**Short answer:** For small to mid-sized hospitals and clinics in India, **SalaryBox** (from ₹27/employee/month) offers the best combination of touchless selfie attendance, shift scheduling, and automated payroll with PF/ESI compliance. For enterprise hospital chains with 1,000+ staff, **Keka** or **Darwinbox** provide deeper multi-entity payroll and advanced workforce analytics. If budget is the primary concern, **greytHR** offers a free plan for up to 25 employees — ideal for standalone clinics.


India’s healthcare sector employs over **5.7 million workers** across roughly **70,000+ hospitals** and **1,50,000+ clinics** , yet most still manage staff attendance on paper registers and process payroll manually in spreadsheets. According to a[2026 payroll technology study](https://blog.petpooja.com/people-payroll/payroll-hr-technology-statistics-india/) , **51% of small businesses still use spreadsheets for payroll** , and the average company makes **15 errors per payroll cycle** — each costing approximately **$291 (₹24,000+) to fix** . In a hospital, where nurses rotate across three shifts and contractual staff change monthly, those errors multiply.


We evaluated **18 HR and attendance platforms** against five healthcare-specific criteria to identify the 10 that work best for Indian hospitals, clinics, diagnostic centres, and nursing homes in 2026.

## How Did We Select the Best Healthcare Attendance & Payroll Software?


We evaluated 18 platforms over 6 weeks using five criteria weighted for healthcare-specific needs:


1. **Shift scheduling depth (25% weight):** Can it handle 24/7 rotational shifts, night-shift allowances, emergency overtime, and skill-based nurse scheduling? Hospitals aren’t 9-to-5 workplaces — the software must reflect that.
2. **Touchless attendance options (20%):** Post-COVID, touchless attendance is non-negotiable in healthcare. We tested selfie verification, GPS geofencing, facial recognition, and contactless biometric integrations.
3. **Payroll accuracy and compliance (25%):** PF, ESI, Professional Tax, TDS — plus the ability to handle different pay structures for permanent nurses, contract doctors, visiting consultants, and part-time housekeeping staff.
4. **Multi-location and department support (15%):** Hospitals have OPDs, ICUs, pharmacies, labs, and admin — each with different shift patterns. Multi-branch hospital chains need centralized dashboards.
5. **Ease of setup and cost (15%):** Smaller clinics can’t afford ₹50,000/month enterprise solutions or 3-month implementation cycles.


Sources included G2 and Capterra reviews (filtered for healthcare use cases), vendor documentation, and direct testing of free trials where available.


## What Are the Best Attendance & Payroll Platforms for Indian Hospitals in 2026?


### 1. SalaryBox — Best for Small to Mid-Sized Hospitals & Clinics


**Quick take:** SalaryBox is an attendance-first platform built for Indian SMEs, offering GPS and selfie check-in, automated shift scheduling, and fully integrated payroll — all starting at ₹80/employee/month. Its mobile-first design makes it especially practical for clinics where staff don’t sit at desks all day.


**Key healthcare features:** SalaryBox supports multi-shift scheduling with rotation templates, which suits hospitals running morning-evening-night rotations. Selfie-based attendance eliminates the hygiene concern of shared biometric devices — staff punch in from their own phones with GPS verification. The payroll engine handles PF, ESI, TDS, and Professional Tax automatically, including different pay structures for permanent and contractual staff. The mobile app (Android and iOS) lets ward managers approve leaves and check attendance without logging into a desktop dashboard.


**Pricing:** ₹80 per employee per month. Free trial available. No minimum employee count requirement.


**Limitations:** SalaryBox works best for hospitals with up to 500 employees. It doesn’t offer AI-driven workforce planning or advanced analytics dashboards that enterprise chains may need. The on-premise deployment option is not available — it’s cloud-only.


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on Google Play Store (12,500+ ratings) · 4.7/5 features on Capterra


*→ Read more:[SalaryBox vs greytHR detailed comparison](https://salarybox.in/blog/salarybox-vs-greythr-honest-comparison-for-small-businesses-in-2026/)*


### 2. greytHR — Best Budget Option for Standalone Clinics


**Quick take:** greytHR offers a genuinely free plan for up to 25 employees with core payroll and attendance — ideal for small clinics, dental practices, and standalone diagnostic centres that need to automate without spending. Paid plans start at ₹3,495/month for larger teams.


**Key healthcare features:** greytHR’s shift roster management supports healthcare rotation patterns, and the shift-swap workflow lets nurses request swaps with manager approval. The payroll engine covers all Indian statutory requirements (PF, ESI, TDS, PT, gratuity) and has been refined over **15+ years in the Indian market** . Geo-fenced attendance works for multi-floor hospitals where you need staff to check in from specific departments. Employee self-service lets staff view payslips, apply for leave, and download Form 16 from their phones.


**Pricing:** Free for up to 25 employees. Paid plans from ₹3,495/month.


**Limitations:** The free plan has limited shift scheduling options. Advanced features like custom reports and multi-entity payroll require premium tiers. The interface feels dated compared to newer platforms. Customer support response times can be slow on the free plan.


**Ratings:** 4.4/5 on G2 (1,000+ reviews) · 4.4/5 on Capterra


*→ Read more:[SalaryBox vs greytHR: Which fits SMEs better?](https://salarybox.in/blog/salarybox-vs-greythr-honest-comparison-for-small-businesses-in-2026/)*


### 3. Keka — Best for Mid-to-Large Hospitals with Complex Payroll


**Quick take:** Keka stands out for hospitals with 200–2,000+ employees that need advanced shift scheduling, multi-entity payroll, and deep performance analytics. Its payroll engine is among the most accurate in India, with automated PF, ESI, and multi-state Professional Tax calculations.


**Key healthcare features:** Keka’s shift management includes auto-fill scheduling that detects gaps when someone calls in sick and suggests replacements based on availability and skills. The platform supports multiple pay groups — critical for hospitals that pay nurses, contractual housekeeping staff, visiting consultants, and resident doctors on completely different structures. Its expense management module handles the reimbursement claims that field-visit nurses and home-care teams generate. According to[Keka’s workforce management guide](https://www.keka.com/healthcare-workforce-management-guide) , replacing a healthcare worker costs **20–33% of their annual salary** , and Keka includes attrition analytics to flag flight-risk employees early.


**Pricing:** From ₹6,999/month + ₹60 per employee. No free plan.


**Limitations:** The price point is steep for clinics under 50 employees. Setup takes 1–2 weeks. The interface has a learning curve — non-technical hospital administrators may struggle initially. No free plan available.


**Ratings:** 4.5/5 on G2 (1,400+ reviews) · 4.5/5 on Capterra


*→ Read more:[SalaryBox vs Keka features and pricing comparison](https://salarybox.in/blog/salarybox-vs-keka-features-pricing-which-is-better-for-smbs-in-2026/)*


### 4. Zoho People — Best for Clinics Already Using the Zoho Ecosystem


**Quick take:** If your hospital already uses Zoho Books, Zoho CRM, or Zoho Mail, Zoho People integrates seamlessly at ₹48/user/month for the attendance module. Its facial recognition attendance and shift scheduling are solid, but payroll requires a separate Zoho Payroll subscription.


**Key healthcare features:** Zoho People supports multi-shift scheduling with weekly and monthly rotation templates. Its facial recognition attendance works on standard smartphones without dedicated hardware. The leave management module handles complex leave types (casual, earned, sick, maternity, compensatory off) that hospitals need. Zoho’s API ecosystem allows integration with hospital management systems. The HR analytics module provides department-wise attendance dashboards.


**Pricing:** ₹48/user/month for the HR + attendance module. Zoho Payroll starts at ₹40/employee/month additionally.


**Limitations:** Payroll and attendance are separate products — you pay twice. The platform works best within the Zoho ecosystem; standalone users miss integration benefits. Shift scheduling is less advanced than Keka or FactoHR for complex healthcare patterns. No healthcare-specific templates out of the box.


**Ratings:** 4.4/5 on G2 (500+ reviews) · 4.4/5 on Capterra


*→ Read more:[SalaryBox vs Zoho People detailed comparison](https://salarybox.in/blog/salarybox-vs-zoho-people-detailed-attendance-timesheet-comparison-2025/)*


### 5. FactoHR — Best Dedicated Healthcare HR Platform


**Quick take:** FactoHR is the only platform on this list with a[dedicated healthcare industry page](https://factohr.com/industries/healthcare/) and pre-built healthcare workflows. Its skill-based auto-scheduling and AI face recognition make it a strong choice for hospitals that want a vendor who actively speaks their language.


**Key healthcare features:** FactoHR’s healthcare module includes skill-based auto-scheduling (assign nurses by ICU certification, OT experience, or department), contract staff management with expiry alerts for licenses and certifications, and contactless AI face recognition attendance. The platform supports **24×7 shift patterns** with night-shift allowances automatically fed into payroll. Retrospective payroll handles late-joining contract staff. Multi-entity support lets hospital chains manage each branch under one dashboard. It holds ISO 27001, SOC 2, and DPDP certifications.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing (quote required). Free demo available.


**Limitations:** No transparent pricing on the website — you must request a quote, which slows decision-making for smaller clinics. No free plan. The interface is feature-rich but can feel overwhelming for single-clinic operations. Implementation for large hospitals may take 2–4 weeks.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 (400+ reviews)


### 6. HROne — Best for Multi-Location Hospital Chains


**Quick take:** HROne serves **2,000+ Indian companies** and is particularly strong for hospital chains operating across multiple cities. Its centralized dashboard lets head office manage attendance, shifts, and payroll across all branches while each location retains flexibility for local policies.


**Key healthcare features:** HROne’s multi-branch shift management allows location-specific shift templates — an ICU in Delhi can run different shift patterns from an OPD in Mumbai, but payroll consolidation happens centrally. Biometric and geo-fenced attendance work for fixed locations, while mobile check-in handles visiting doctors and home-care staff. The payroll engine manages multi-state compliance automatically, which matters for hospital chains operating across states with different Professional Tax slabs.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing based on employee count and modules.


**Limitations:** Not ideal for standalone clinics under 50 employees — the platform is built for scale. No transparent pricing. The mobile app interface has received mixed reviews on app stores. Limited self-service customisation for non-technical HR staff.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 (800+ reviews)


*→ Read more:[SalaryBox vs HROne attendance tracking comparison](https://salarybox.in/blog/salarybox-vs-hrone-which-offers-better-attendance-tracking/)*


### 7. Pocket HRMS — Best for Hospitals Wanting an AI Chatbot for HR Queries


**Quick take:** Pocket HRMS differentiates itself with **smHRty** , an AI-powered chatbot that handles employee HR queries — leave balance, payslip downloads, shift information, without involving the HR team. For hospitals where the HR department is stretched thin (often just 1–2 people managing 200+ staff), this feature saves hours weekly.


**Key healthcare features:** Shift roster management supports healthcare rotation patterns. Selfie and geo-tagged attendance verify that staff are checking in from the hospital premises. The payroll module covers PF, ESI, TDS, and Professional Tax. The AI chatbot handles routine queries that otherwise flood the HR inbox — particularly useful during shift changes when nurses need quick answers about overtime calculations or leave balances.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing. Free demo available.


**Limitations:** The platform’s core attendance and payroll features are competent but not as deep as Keka or FactoHR for complex healthcare scenarios. Shift auto-fill and skill-based scheduling are basic. Limited multi-entity support. The AI chatbot, while useful, occasionally misinterprets complex queries.


**Ratings:** 4.3/5 on G2 (200+ reviews)


*→ Read more:[SalaryBox vs Pocket HRMS review](https://salarybox.in/blog/salarybox-vs-pocket-hrms-review-which-one-should-your-business-use/)*


### 8. Darwinbox — Best Enterprise Platform for Large Hospital Chains


**Quick take:** Darwinbox is the premium choice for large hospital chains and healthcare groups with 1,000+ employees across multiple locations. Its AI-driven workforce planning, advanced analytics, and enterprise-grade integrations set it apart — but the price and implementation timeline put it out of reach for smaller operations.


**Key healthcare features:** Darwinbox offers AI-driven workforce demand forecasting that predicts staffing needs based on seasonal patterns — useful for hospitals that see predictable spikes during monsoon season or flu waves. Multi-entity payroll handles complex structures: different CTC components for doctors versus support staff, different PF slabs across states, different overtime rules per department. Face recognition and iris scanning attendance provide top-tier identity verification. The analytics dashboard provides real-time visibility into department-wise attendance, overtime costs, and absenteeism trends.


**Pricing:** Custom enterprise pricing (typically for 500+ employees). No free plan.


**Limitations:** Expensive for any operation under 500 employees. Implementation takes 4–8 weeks. The platform’s depth means a steeper learning curve for hospital administrators. Overkill for standalone clinics or nursing homes.


**Ratings:** 4.4/5 on G2 (600+ reviews)


### 9. sumHR — Most Affordable Option for Small Nursing Homes


**Quick take:** At ₹49/employee/month, sumHR is the lowest-cost paid platform on this list. It covers the basics, selfie attendance, GPS check-in, leave management, and payroll with PF/ESI/TDS making it practical for small nursing homes and single-doctor clinics that just need to get off spreadsheets.


**Key healthcare features:** Selfie and GPS-based attendance verification is clean and simple. The shift management module handles basic morning-evening-night rotations. Payroll automates PF, ESI, and TDS calculations. The employee self-service portal lets staff check attendance records and download payslips without bothering the admin. The platform’s simplicity is its biggest advantage — setup takes less than a day for a small team.


**Pricing:** From ₹49/employee/month.


**Limitations:** Limited shift scheduling depth — no auto-fill, no skill-based assignment, no complex rotation templates. No advanced analytics or workforce planning. Multi-location support is basic. Not suitable for hospitals above 200 employees. Limited third-party integrations.


**Ratings:** 4.3/5 on G2 (100+ reviews)


### 10. Spine HR — Best for Hospitals Needing an On-Premise Deployment Option


**Quick take:** Spine HR is the only platform on this list that offers both cloud and on-premise deployment. For government hospitals, defence medical facilities, or institutions with strict data residency requirements, the on-premise option is a genuine differentiator that cloud-only platforms can’t match.


**Key healthcare features:** Spine HR supports shift scheduling with overtime tracking, biometric device integration (all major Indian brands), and a comprehensive payroll engine with full statutory compliance. Its reporting module generates custom MIS reports — useful for hospital management boards that need specific formats. The on-premise version stores all employee data on the hospital’s own servers, addressing data sovereignty concerns that some healthcare institutions have about cloud storage.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing for both cloud and on-premise deployments.


**Limitations:** The interface is the least modern on this list. Mobile app features lag behind cloud-native competitors. On-premise deployment requires IT infrastructure and maintenance. No AI-powered features. Limited self-service capabilities for employees. Updates to the on-premise version require manual installation.


**Ratings:** 4.2/5 on Capterra


## Which Attendance & Payroll Software Should Your Hospital Choose?


The right choice depends on your hospital’s size, budget, and complexity:


**For small clinics and nursing homes (10–50 employees):** Start with **greytHR** if budget is the #1 constraint (free for up to 25) or **SalaryBox** (₹80/employee/month) for better shift scheduling and selfie attendance. Both can be set up in a day.


**For mid-sized hospitals (50–500 employees):** **SalaryBox** or **FactoHR** are your best options. SalaryBox offers simpler setup and transparent pricing. FactoHR provides deeper healthcare-specific features like skill-based scheduling and certification tracking, but requires a quote.


**For large hospital chains (500–2,000+ employees):** **Keka** for multi-entity payroll and advanced analytics, or **Darwinbox** if you need AI-driven workforce planning and can absorb the enterprise pricing and implementation timeline.


**For multi-location chains needing centralized control:** **HROne** provides the strongest centralized dashboard with location-specific policy flexibility.


**For Zoho ecosystem users:** **Zoho People** is the natural fit, but budget for Zoho Payroll separately.


**For government or data-sensitive hospitals needing on-premise:** **Spine HR** is your only option on this list with on-premise deployment.


## Why Do Indian Hospitals Need Dedicated Attendance & Payroll Software in 2026?


India’s healthcare workforce is under unprecedented pressure. The country has just **1.7 nurses per 1,000 people** and **1 doctor per 1,500 people** , according to a[Keka workforce management report](https://www.keka.com/healthcare-workforce-management-guide) . Demand for healthcare professionals is projected to **double by 2030** , with a supply shortfall of roughly **10 million workers** ([People Matters](https://www.peoplematters.in/article/performance-management/addressing-the-shortage-of-healthcare-professionals-in-india-45073) ). About **75% of India’s healthcare infrastructure** is concentrated in urban areas, serving just 27% of the population.


In this environment, manual attendance tracking and spreadsheet payroll create problems that directly affect patient care:


- **Shift scheduling errors** lead to understaffed wards — studies link nurse understaffing to higher rates of medication errors and patient falls.
- **Payroll disputes** over overtime, night-shift allowances, and incorrect deductions are a top driver of nursing staff attrition. Replacing a healthcare worker costs **20–33% of their annual salary** .
- **Compliance penalties:** **53% of companies have paid statutory non-compliance penalties** (PF, ESI, TDS), and **1 in 6 has faced litigation over payroll errors** ([Petpooja, citing G2 2025](https://blog.petpooja.com/people-payroll/payroll-hr-technology-statistics-india/) ).
- **Time theft:** Time and attendance errors average **1,139 per 1,000 employees annually** , and time theft costs up to **7% of gross annual payroll** ([Verified Market Reports via Petpooja](https://blog.petpooja.com/people-payroll/payroll-hr-technology-statistics-india/) ).


Automated systems reduce payroll error rates from **1–8% (manual) to below 1%** , cut compliance issues by **70%** , and reduce processing time by up to **80%** ([G2, 2025; Select Software Reviews, 2026](https://blog.petpooja.com/people-payroll/payroll-hr-technology-statistics-india/) ).

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Which is the best attendance software for hospitals in India?


For small to mid-sized hospitals and clinics (up to 500 staff), **SalaryBox** offers the best balance of healthcare-relevant features GPS and selfie attendance, shift scheduling, and automated payroll with PF/ESI compliance ,starting at ₹80 per employee per month. For large hospital chains with 1,000+ employees, **Darwinbox** or **Keka** offer deeper enterprise-grade shift management and multi-entity payroll.


### How does shift scheduling work in healthcare attendance software?


Healthcare attendance software lets administrators create rotating shift patterns (morning, evening, night), assign staff by department or skill, enable shift swaps with manager approval, and auto-fill gaps when someone calls in sick. The best platforms also track overtime hours automatically and feed shift data directly into payroll for accurate night-shift and overtime allowances.


### What attendance method works best in hospitals, biometric or app-based?


App-based attendance using selfie verification or GPS check-in is increasingly preferred over biometric devices in healthcare settings. Touchless methods reduce infection risk a critical concern in hospitals. Selfie-based attendance also works for home-visit nurses and field staff who cannot access a fixed biometric terminal. Many hospitals use a hybrid approach: biometric at the main entrance plus app-based check-in for ward and field staff.


### Is payroll automation worth it for a small clinic with 20–30 employees?


Yes. Even for small clinics, automated payroll eliminates manual errors that average **15 per payroll cycle** and cost **₹24,000+ each to fix** ([G2, 2025](https://blog.petpooja.com/people-payroll/payroll-hr-technology-statistics-india/) ). With PF, ESI, and TDS calculations automated, a 30-employee clinic saves roughly 8–12 hours per month on payroll processing alone. Platforms like SalaryBox and greytHR offer plans starting under ₹3,500 per month for small teams.


### Do these software platforms comply with Indian labour laws for healthcare workers?


Most platforms on this list handle core Indian statutory compliance, PF, ESI, Professional Tax, TDS, and gratuity. However, healthcare-specific regulations like the Clinical Establishments Act and state-level nursing home rules may require manual compliance tracking. Platforms like **FactoHR** and **Keka** allow custom compliance rule configuration. Always verify that your chosen software covers the specific state-level labour rules applicable to your hospital.


### Can attendance software handle different employee types in a hospital?


Yes. Hospitals typically employ permanent staff, contractual workers, visiting consultants, and part-time nurses — each with different pay structures and attendance rules. The best platforms ( **SalaryBox, FactoHR, Keka, greytHR** ) support custom employee categories with separate payroll rules, attendance policies, and leave types for each group.


### What is the average cost of attendance and payroll software for hospitals in India?


For Indian healthcare businesses, attendance and payroll software typically costs between **₹40 and ₹200 per employee per month** . Budget options like greytHR (free for up to 25 employees) and SalaryBox (₹80/employee/month) suit small clinics. Mid-range platforms like Keka (from ₹6,999/month) and Zoho People (₹48/user/month for attendance) work for mid-sized hospitals. Enterprise platforms like Darwinbox provide custom pricing for large hospital chains.


### How long does it take to implement attendance software in a hospital?


Implementation timelines vary by hospital size and software complexity. Cloud-based platforms like **SalaryBox** and **Zoho People** can be set up in 1–3 days for small clinics. Mid-range platforms like Keka and greytHR typically take 1–2 weeks for hospitals with 100–500 employees. Enterprise platforms like Darwinbox may require 4–8 weeks for large hospital chains with complex shift patterns, multi-location setups, and custom integrations.
